history.summary: Ancient Shiva temple in Uttareshwar Peth, Kolhapur, a short distance from Rankala Lake. It is noted locally for housing one of the largest Shivlingas in West Maharashtra and is described by visitors as a peaceful, old holy place. NOTE: travel sites (e.g. myadhyatm, lightuptemples) conflate this Kolhapur temple with a separate 5th-6th-century brick-and-wood Uttareshwar Mahadev Temple at Ter in Osmanabad (Dharashiv) district; the two are different temples. Antiquity claims for the Kolhapur temple (one online review claims 1,700 years / Pandava era) are UNVERIFIED.

name: Uttareshwar Mahadev Temple
town_description: Kolhapur is a historic city in southwestern Maharashtra on the banks of the Panchganga river. It was the capital of the Maratha princely state of Kolhapur and remains a major religious centre, home to the famed Mahalaxmi (Ambabai) temple, Rankala Lake and the New Palace. The city is also known for Kolhapuri chappals, its kushti (wrestling) tradition and distinctive cuisine.

travel.road: Within Kolhapur city at Uttareshwar Peth (M6X8+Q6V), ~0.8 km from Rankala Lake
